hints: Focus on what each reagent does in sequence, first cold dilute KMnO4 on an alkene, then conc H2SO4 on that product.
Draw the diol formed from (CH3)2C=C(CH3)CH2CH3 and note which carbons have H atoms available for later removal.
Think about losing two water molecules to give C7H12 and check which diene names are chemically possible with correct valency.
walkthrough:
**Form the diol with cold KMnO4**

Cold, dilute KMnO4 gives syn dihydroxylation of the C=C bond. Each C of the double bond gains one OH group.

$$ (CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3)CH_2CH_3 + [O] + H_2O \rightarrow (CH_3)_2C(OH)-C(OH)(CH_3)CH_2CH_3 $$
This is 2,3-dimethylpentane-2,3-diol, formula $C_7H_{16}O_2$.

**Dehydrate twice with conc H2SO4**

Excess concentrated $H_2SO_4$ at $180^{\circ}C$ is a strong dehydrating agent. It removes $H_2O$ from alcohols by removing OH and a H from a neighbouring carbon.

$$ C_7H_{16}O_2 - 2H_2O \rightarrow C_7H_{12} $$
So both OH groups are lost and two new C=C bonds form, giving a diene.

**Work out where the new double bonds can form**

C2 has no H, it has two $CH_3$ groups plus C3. So loss of C2-OH must take H from C1, giving $C1=C2$.
C3 has no H on C2 side that is useful, but C4 is $CH_2$. Loss of C3-OH with H from C4 gives $C3=C4$.
Product is therefore $CH_2=C(CH_3)-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3$.

**Name the diene and spot isomerism**

$CH_2=C(CH_3)-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3$ is 2,3-dimethylpenta-1,3-diene. The $C3=C4$ bond has two different groups at each end, so cis and trans isomers exist. One of the mixture is therefore cis-2,3-dimethylpenta-1,3-diene.

options.A: 2,3-dimethylpenta-1,2-diene would require C1=C2 and C2=C3, a cumulated allene with methyls on C2 and C3. C2 would then have five bonds (two doubles plus a methyl), which is impossible. It cannot form from this diol.
options.B: This is CH2=C(CH3)-C(CH3)=CH-CH3, exactly formed by C1=C2 from dehydration at C2 and C3=C4 from dehydration at C3. The C3=C4 bond shows cis-trans isomerism, so the cis isomer is a valid product with formula C7H12.
options.C: 2,3-dimethylpenta-1,4-diene would need double bonds at C1=C2 and C4=C5. The second double bond at C4=C5 cannot form because the OH is on C3, not C4. Dehydration at C3 with H from C4 gives C3=C4, not C4=C5.
options.D: 3,4-dimethylpenta-1,3-diene is CH2=CH-C(CH3)=C(CH3)-CH3. This needs an unsubstituted C2 in the C1=C2 bond, but our C2 must keep its methyl group from the starting material. The correct numbering of the actual product is 2,3- not 3,4-.
